owner_directive_4991.primary_citation: Alan K. Mackworth, Consistency in Networks of Relations, Artificial Intelligence 8(1), 99–118, 1977
owner_directive_4991.behavior: Given finite named variables X, finite ordered enumerated domains D(X), and explicitly directed binary relations R(X,Y) of allowed pairs, monotonically delete any x in D(X) having no current y in D(Y) with (x,y) in every arc from X to Y. Return the unique greatest subdomain fixpoint independent of revision order, sorted by variable/value, together with ARC-CONSISTENT when all remaining domains are nonempty, otherwise EMPTY-DOMAIN-CONTRADICTION. An absent reverse arc is not synthesized. Input is immutable, any missing variable or malformed relation is invalid. Local consistency does not assert existence of a complete assignment.
owner_directive_4991.arity: (finite named domain map, directed allowed-pair arcs)->(fixedpoint domain map, local-consistency status)

positive_witnesses.expected: all domains remain {0,1}; ARC-CONSISTENT despite globally unsatisfiable network

falsifiers: Reverse directed relation cannot be inferred when only one directed arc is present.
No support under current target domain must remove a source value, including chained re-revision.
Nonempty arc-consistent odd binary inequality cycle is not globally SAT; report only local consistency.
Duplicate input arcs and different arc schedules cannot change greatest fixpoint.
Original input domain mapping and relations are never modified.
A contradictory empty domain must not be reported ARC-CONSISTENT.
Unification equality/term substitution, ATMS support-label, STRIPS regression and global backtracking solver do not have the same observable input/output law.
